chunks: A number of our people narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Sa'idah, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent me to a woman from the family of al-Zubayr to look at her, as he intended to marry her. When I entered upon her, she spoke to me softly, then said, 'Bring the lamp closer.' I brought it closer to her. Sa'idah said, 'I looked at her, and there was someone else with Sa'idah as well,' and asked, 'Are you pleased?' He said that Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) married her, and she remained with him until he died. When that reached his slave-girls, they began to pull at his sleeves and clothes, while he remained silent, smiling, and saying nothing to them. It is mentioned that he said, 'No thing is like free women.'

key_terms.آلِ زُبَيْرٍ: Family of al-Zubayr, a prominent Arab lineage
key_terms.الْحَرَائِرِ: Free women (as opposed to slave women)
key_terms.لأنْظُرَ إِلَيْهَا: To look at her (for marriage inspection)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about free women compared to slave women?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of marital selection criteria in Shia tradition, where the Imam delegates the inspection of a potential spouse to a trusted female companion, Sa'idah, to ensure suitability. The narrative concludes with a notable remark on the social distinction between free women (al-hara'ir) and slave women, reflecting the status of the Imam's household and the value placed on lineage and freedom in marital unions.
